Eva is saving money to buy a ticket to Tokyo. People around Eva often share different ideas about the airport. Eva bought a T-shirt online because it was much cheaper. We take a walk on the beach.

They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The airport looked quieter than usual that evening. Lily always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Best of all, the train went through a long tunnel.
What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. At first, Eva found it difficult to keep the habit. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. Best of all, the hovercraft skims the wetlands.
Eva plans to study English harder this term. Eva thanked Lily for the honest advice. The experience taught Eva more than any book could. Also, a house swap made the Tokyo stay affordable.
There are always more possibilities than we expect. On Thursday evenings, Eva reviews the notes from class. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right.
